speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg; to begin our assessment, how long has this lesion been present and did you start it with any injury or insect bite?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cutaneous Leishmaniasis.

The history of a painful, ulcerative leg lesion appearing one month after an ant bite, combined with significant immunosuppression from Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes, and recent steroid use, strongly suggests a parasitic infection. Given the specific vector (ant) and the patient's compromised immune system, please confirm if you have any history of travel to endemic regions like the Mediterranean, Middle East, or Central/South America. REQUEST TEST: Blood smear for Leishmania parasites. REQUEST IMAGES: Lesion photograph of the right leg ulcer.
